reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode through Nov 2, data fresh (not stale): SPX -3.86% from its 120-day high, -1.99% below its 50-day but +3.13% above its 200-day; SMH -24.34% from its high and between zones at $508.31, NVDA in Zone 1 at $202.06; VIX 21.15 at its 5-day high, HY OAS 3.43 calm; mechanical tally 2 of 4 — zone occupancy and credit calm confirmed, no volume climax, no VIX rollover.
reaction.invalidation: SMH reclaiming and holding above $580-600 (the failure zone) with SPX back above $7,750-7,820 voids the correction thesis; HY OAS breaking above 4% voids the rotation thesis and turns this into a credit event. Either one cancels the stance and the ladder.

ladder.response: Arm Tranche A preparation: verify the capitulation tally and size per the ladder. Do not deploy on the print alone — the print is the trigger leg, not the confirmation.
ladder.trigger: SMH closes inside Zone 2 ($470-505), with NVDA moving toward $175-185

ladder.response: Treat it as a sell-the-rally zone, not a buy signal. No chasing, no new adds; wait for the low to be re-tested before any entry.
ladder.trigger: SPX bounces into the $7,750-7,820 failure zone and stalls or fails

ladder.response: Stand down: no deployment, preserve bills, re-audit zones and ratios. The correction thesis becomes a bear-market thesis and the ladder is void until re-audited.
ladder.trigger: HY OAS closes above 4% or VIX closes above 25, or SMH closes below $470 (under Zone 2)

ladder.response: Deploy Tranche A per the ladder at Zone 2 prints — this is the re-entry condition the correction has not yet met.
ladder.trigger: Failed first bounce plus a second low holding, with the mechanical tally at 3+ of 4 (volume climax reversal and VIX rollover confirmed) and the 10-year falling

reaction.trapRisk: Today's midday bounce (SPY +0.56%, QQQ +0.91%, VIX -3.4%) is the classic pivot-and-fail setup: SMH is still between zones, NVDA still in Zone 1, and neither unconfirmed tally signal (volume climax, VIX rollover) has printed. Entries sized on this bounce buy the trap. Wait for the failure-zone retest verdict at SPX $7,750-7,820 or a Zone 2 print before sizing anything.

strategyPosture: Watch with a probe list ready: the correction is real (SMH -24.34% from its high, NVDA in Zone 1) but no tranche trigger has printed — SMH sits $3 above Zone 2, the mechanical tally is 2 of 4, and today's midday bounce is unconfirmed. New money stays in bills; nothing gets sized until a zone prints or the bounce confirms.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real and the leadership fracture inside Mag 7 matters — GOOGL and MSFT are 26 points apart — but the credit data says rotation, not systemic rollover. The read flips if the gap keeps widening while lending or spreads tighten; until then, index-level calm is not a lie, it is a rotation.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag 7 averages -15.71% from 52-week highs against SPY at -3.2%, a -12.51 point divergence gap; SPX itself is only -3.86% off its 120-day high (7,541.4 close Nov 2). Bank lending standards are LOOSE at 1.7% on SLOOS, far below the ~40% stress threshold, and HY OAS is 3.43 and calm. The weakest Mag 7 name is GOOGL at -31.7% from its high; the strongest is MSFT at -5.4%.
themes.label: Mag 7 rotation, not rollover
themes.narrative: The Mag 7 selloff reads as a broad market rollover: the names that dominate the index by weight are falling hard while the index itself looks calm.
themes.watchFor: Mag 7-SPX divergence gap widening past 15 points, or SLOOS/HY OAS breaking toward stress levels.

themes.counterRead: Growth does not set the floor — the tape is pricing financing costs (10-year 4.94%, fed funds 3.88%) and multiple compression (AMAT, KLAC both tagged MULTIPLE_COMPRESSION). No buy zone has printed: SMH at $508.31 sits $3 above Zone 2's top ($505), NVDA is in Zone 1 not Zone 2, and MU at $852.99 is far above its $700-745 Zone 2. The setup is real; the entry is not yet.
themes.dataAnchor: Revenue growth has not broken: NVDA revenue +61.4% year over year at $207.61, -14.7% from its high and sitting in Zone 1 ($200-210); AVGO revenue +55% year over year with a 42.1% free-cash-flow margin, -32.8% from its high, the top conviction promotion at score 80-81; LRCX revenue +131.3% year over year, -47.5% from its high; DDOG carries an 80% gross margin and $1,001M free cash flow, -27.1% from its high. MU is the exception on catalyst, tagged ACUTE_CATALYST at $852.99, -32% from its high.
themes.label: AI complex: fundamentals ahead of price
themes.narrative: The AI trade is unwinding as a financing bubble: SMH is -24.34% from its high and -19.81% in 20 days, TQQQ -26.6% in a month, and the whole complex is priced as if demand broke.
themes.watchFor: SMH closing inside Zone 2 ($470-505) or NVDA closing inside Zone 2 ($175-185).

themes.counterRead: One research note and one green day do not repair a 30%+ monthly drawdown in SMR/OKLO, and the dislocation table still tags the power leg SENTIMENT_DRIVEN — except VST, whose revenue inflection reads DETERIORATING despite $1.17M of insider buying at the trough. The fear narrative overshot, but the demand story still needs verification before the bounce becomes a turn.
themes.dataAnchor: SMR is -30.92% and OKLO -35.51% over one month; VRT is -38.2% from its 52-week high at $234.66 and ETN -18.1%. But on Election Day itself Bernstein called the data-center fears overblown, with Vertiv up 6% and Eaton up 7% on the day, and the broader tape bounced with it (SPY +0.56%, QQQ +0.91% midday). The election event carries 12 headline hits at MEDIUM signal strength.
themes.label: Election-day data-center fear, walked back same day
themes.narrative: Midterm election risk is hitting the AI data-center buildout — the power and infrastructure leg fell hardest over the past month on election uncertainty.
themes.watchFor: VRT holding above $234.66 through the week and SMR/OKLO printing a higher low instead of a new monthly low.

themes.counterRead: Fear is still elevated even as credit is calm — VIX at its 5-day high says the market is not relaxed, just not frozen. If HY OAS breaks above 4% the read flips from repricing to credit event and the rotation thesis dies with it. The December 8-9 FOMC is already an anticipated HIGH-signal event.
themes.dataAnchor: HY OAS is 3.43, flagged calm and not cracking; bank lending standards are LOOSE at 1.7%; the 10-year is 4.94% with the 2s10s curve at +0.38, upward-sloping rather than inverted; fed funds at 3.88%. The stress is a growth and financing repricing in equities, not a funding freeze. VIX closed Nov 2 at 21.15, its 5-day high, and sits 20.43 midday, -3.4% on the day.
themes.label: Credit calm while equities reprice
themes.narrative: A -24% SMH drawdown and VIX up 36% in 20 days smells like a credit event in the making — the kind of stress that turns a correction into something worse.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS closing above 4% or VIX closing above 25 — the stand-down line.

A Zone 2 print there, or NVDA sliding from Zone 1 ($200-210) toward $185, converts this correction from watch to deployment; until then the wave is a bounce into the SPX $7,750-7,820 failure zone, which is the trap to avoid chasing.
